sections.text: Each week, I come up with three science news items or facts, two real and one fake. And then I challenge my panel of skeptics to tell me which one is the fake. We have a theme this week. The theme is adapting to climate change.

I'm just-
As soon as you said it.
I knew it just now.
I thought it was going to be adapting to Florida. For Cara.

OK, so there's a three things that people are working on or have proposed or whatever that to adapt to the changes of the climate. OK, here we go. Item #1: Scientists at the University of the Philippines have proposed burying plastic waste beneath sinking islands to keep them above water. Item #2: China is at the forefront of building sponge cities, cities that incorporate features that absorb large amounts of water to help reduce storm water damage. And item #3: A glaciologist at Princeton University has proposed building massive miles long seawalls at the bases of Antarctic and Greenland glaciers in order to delay their collapse, perhaps by hundreds of years. Bob, you seem eager to go. So why don't you go first?
Oh, god, man. This is so. All right. Plastic waste beneath sinking islands,. How? Does that make any, fiction, fiction! Done!
You're not even going to consider the other two? All right.
This is ridiculous.
Wow.
All right, Evan?

Nope.

So that means drilling holes into the bedrock or to the wherever the, it that wouldn't work. Would that work? I don't even really I don't even know how that's plausible to tell you the truth. Not that that wouldn't be the case. But it doesn't make it not science. But geez, that's like a big zero in my book as well. But the other ones about the sponge cities in China, incorporating features that absorb large amounts of water to help reduce storm water damage, I think this has been attempted before. I seem to recall reading something about this years ago. I don't know if it was China or somewhere else, but there was the talk of using sponges to do just this to absorb water. So I think that one's at least I've got some reference on that one. The last one about the glaciologist. That's neat that that's a thing. Proposed building massive miles long sea walls at the bases of Antarctic and Greenland glaciers in order to delay their collapse. Well, yeah, I mean, but again, there's a basis for this. They are they do build seawalls all over the world in various climates and with the idea of protection. In a long, much more long winded way. I agree with Bob.
OK. Cara?
It means fiction.

They proposed it. They also proposed throwing a paper airplane to the Moon to see if it reaches the Moon.

Exactly. So it's like there could be some really out there scientists in the Philippines who are like, I know because there is a plastic waste problem in the Philippines. And that's the idea here. I mean, this is what we saw happening in Houston, just around the world when they're devastating hurricanes and stuff like that. And the cities are all concrete. They just drown. All right. And Jay.

All right. Well, let's start with number two. Since you all agree on that one.

And that one is science. Yep. They're trying to do that. So what's a sponge city? What would that involve? It involves using so called just green roofs, rain gardens, wetlands and other measures. Basically, you want to create an environment that can absorb a lot of water rather than just all blacktop and cement that repels the water so that it can't go anywhere and it builds up. Now, this would be given the degree of flooding, for example, that is being experienced in Florida, these kind of measures wouldn't be enough. So if we could prevent them from collapse, that would be huge.

He's got to convince somebody to spend a lot of money. The idea is he would, like, fill it in with gravel and then put large boulders on the outside of it so that it doesn't erode away. And then basically just keeping back the warm water so it doesn't erode away the glacier. So this was one of the rare times when I had a totally failed science or fiction concept. And I was running out of time, so I basically had to come up with something. But I'm trying to figure out no matter how I searched for it, no matter what my usual terms that I use to find stuff, I kept getting serious scientific papers and not any crazy stuff. So I wonder if it just doesn't exist. And my hypothesis is that the crazy people don't believe in climate change. They're not the ones who are coming up with ways to mitigate it.
